title: How to Write Your First CV for Jobs in Nigeria: Complete Guide
excerpt: Step-by-step guide to creating your first CV as a Nigerian graduate. Get noticed by employers with our proven template and tips.
author: ElevateResume

body.text: Landing your first job in Nigeria can feel overwhelming, especially when you're staring at a blank document wondering how to write your very first CV. As a fresh graduate or young professional, you might think you don't have enough experience to fill a page. The truth is, every Nigerian professional started exactly where you are now.
This comprehensive guide will walk you through creating a compelling first CV that gets you noticed by Nigerian employers, even without extensive work experience.
Understanding the Nigerian Job Market for Fresh Graduates

The Nigerian job market is highly competitive, with thousands of graduates competing for limited entry-level positions. According to the National Bureau of Statistics, youth unemployment in Nigeria remains a significant challenge. However, this doesn't mean opportunities don't exist.

Major Nigerian employers like Dangote Group, MTN Nigeria, First Bank, Access Bank, and PwC Nigeria actively recruit fresh graduates through graduate trainee programs and entry-level positions. These companies receive thousands of applications, making it crucial that your CV stands out from the crowd.
Nigerian employers typically spend less than 30 seconds scanning each CV initially. Your first CV needs to make an immediate positive impression.
Essential Sections for Your First Nigerian CV
Personal Information Section
Start your CV with your personal details at the top. In Nigeria, include:

items: Full name (as it appears on official documents)
Phone number (ensure it's active and professional)
Email address (create a professional one if needed: firstname.lastname@gmail.com)
Home address (city and state are sufficient)
Date of birth (common practice in Nigeria)

body.text: Avoid including your photograph unless specifically requested, as many modern Nigerian companies prefer CVs without photos to reduce unconscious bias.
Professional Summary or Objective
As a first-time job seeker, use an objective statement that clearly communicates your career goals and what you bring to the table. Keep it to 2-3 sentences maximum.

Example: "Recent Economics graduate from University of Lagos seeking an entry-level analyst position in the banking sector. Equipped with strong analytical skills, proficiency in financial modeling, and passion for Nigeria's financial services industry. Eager to contribute to organizational growth while developing professional expertise."
Education Section: Your Strongest Asset
For fresh graduates, education is typically your strongest section. Include:

items: Class of degree (First Class, Second Class Upper, etc.)
Relevant coursework if it relates to your target job

body.text: NYSC Information
If you've completed or are currently serving, include your NYSC details:

items: Place of primary assignment if relevant to your career goals

body.text: Many Nigerian employers prefer candidates who have completed NYSC, so highlight this prominently if applicable.
Skills Section: Showcase Your Potential
Even without extensive work experience, you possess valuable skills. Divide your skills into categories:
Technical Skills

items: Software proficiency (Microsoft Office Suite, especially Excel)

body.text: Soft Skills
Language Skills
In Nigeria's diverse environment, language skills are valuable:

items: Local languages (Hausa, Igbo, Yoruba, or others)

Don't underestimate your accomplishments. Include:

body.text: Formatting Your Nigerian CV for Success
Length and Structure
For fresh graduates in Nigeria, a 1-2 page CV is ideal. Nigerian employers typically prefer concise, well-organized CVs that are easy to scan quickly.
Font and Design
Use professional fonts like:
Keep font size between 10-12 points for body text and slightly larger for headings.
File Format
Always save and send your CV as a PDF to preserve formatting. Name your file professionally: "FirstName_LastName_CV.pdf"
Common Mistakes to Avoid
Spelling and Grammar Errors
Nothing kills a first impression faster than typos. Proofread multiple times and ask someone else to review your CV.
Using Unprofessional Email Addresses
Replace emails like "partylover123@yahoo.com" with professional alternatives.
Including Irrelevant Information
Avoid including:

items: Primary and secondary school details (unless applying for teaching positions)

body.text: Generic Objective Statements
Avoid cliché phrases like "seeking a challenging position" or "dynamic team player."

Making Your CV ATS-Friendly
Many Nigerian companies now use Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) to screen CVs. To ensure your CV passes through:

items: Include relevant keywords from job descriptions
Avoid complex formatting, graphics, or tables
Save as PDF or Word document as specified
Use bullet points for easy scanning

body.text: Research the specific company and role before applying. Tailor your CV keywords to match the job description while remaining truthful about your experiences.
Cover Letter Considerations
While this guide focuses on CVs, many Nigerian employers expect a cover letter. Keep it concise, professional, and specific to the role and company.

body.text: Writing your first CV as a Nigerian job seeker doesn't have to be daunting. Remember that every successful professional started where you are now. Focus on presenting your potential, demonstrating your willingness to learn, and showing how you can contribute to an employer's success.

Your first job might not be your dream role, but it's the crucial first step in building your career in Nigeria's dynamic economy. With a well-crafted CV that highlights your strengths and potential, you're positioning yourself for success in the competitive Nigerian job market.
